title: MECLA: Memory-Compute-Efficient LLM Accelerator with Scaling Sub-matrix Partition
problem: LLM inference requires massive memory footprints and computation, especially from linear layers; generating 32 tokens with LLaMA-7B requires 14GB of weights and 400B+ operations, exceeding consumer-level GPU capabilities.
motivation: Deploying LLMs from cloud to edge requires efficient inference accelerators that can handle prohibitive memory and compute requirements.
method: MECLA uses Scaling Sub-matrix Partition (SSMP) to decompose large weight matrices into source sub-matrices (SS) and derived sub-matrices (DS) obtained by scaling SS with scalars, eliminating full matrix access. On-chip optimizations exploit intermediate data reuse through matrix regrouping, inner-product multiplication re-association, and outer-product partial sum reuse, achieving 83.6% memory access reduction and 72.2% computation reduction.
key_novelty: Parameter-efficient weight matrix decomposition via scaling sub-matrix partition where derived sub-matrices are obtained by scaling source sub-matrices with scalars.
contributions: Scaling Sub-matrix Partition (SSMP) method for decomposing large weight matrices into source and derived sub-matrices
On-chip optimization techniques exploiting intermediate data reuse through matrix regrouping and partial sum reuse
MECLA hardware accelerator achieving 7088 GOPS/W energy efficiency
Evaluation on 20 benchmarks showing 113.14× higher energy efficiency vs V100 and 12.99× vs SpAtten

metrics.speedup: 113.14× vs V100, 12.99× vs SpAtten, 1.62× vs FACT

primary_theme: Memory and compute efficient LLM inference through scaled sub-matrix partitioning
